rih.review:
Best for learning & grading.
He is very easy going, student friendly, well-behaved and supportive. The curving is approximately 10√x.

Overall, he is not a bad faculty member. In terms of teaching, he relies heavily on slides and explains every line. However, because the slides are quite detailed and his lectures can be a bit monotonous, the classes might feel boring. I recommend staying focused and taking notes on what he says, as those details often appear on exams. If you are already proficient in programming and familiar with Object-Oriented Programming (OOP), you won't need to worry much. Otherwise, practice coding on your own and pay close attention in class, regardless of how slow it gets.
He takes three quizzes and counts the best two scores. The quiz questions usually require writing small programs based on a question, which are easy if you practice at home. His midterm and final exams consist of 20 multiple-choice questions (MCQs) and 20 to 30 marks worth of coding problems. The MCQs are quite tricky, so you need to read the slides thoroughly and listen carefully in class to do well. The coding portion is manageable if you understand Java and OOP principles.
He curves the final grades, usually applying 10 root x. He also assigns two assignments, which you should complete independently. Finally, avoid using your phone during class, as he strongly dislikes it. Regarding attendance, showing up 40 to 50 minutes late may result in being marked absent since he takes attendance manually; however, he usually starts his class 20 to 30 minutes after the scheduled start time.
And if you wanna get an A under him, self study java and OOP and keep coding and make projects on our own in java even if it's not required as that's the only way you'll actually learn.

sfr1.review: Sfr1 best for learning and grading

SFR1 sir is one of the best faculty . He really makes the study easy for the student. For learning , he is the best choice. He will explain the topics and always ready for qustions. Don't hesitate to ask questions. He will try his best to answer your question and explain the problem again and again if he has to .

You should feel lucky that you got the chance to do CSE215 under SFR1. He is a highly knowledgeable and skilled faculty. By the way, he won't show the very basics of Java. But, if you have a good grasp of the topics taught in CSE115, you are good to go. His teaching is mostly based on theory. On very rare occasions, he will code in front of the students (sometimes, he might not at all). But trust me, if you are good at the basics, those theories will help a lot. His questions are standard (some people might find it extremely difficult). He mostly gives theory questions, but he also puts some programming problems. You have to be super prepared and efficient to ace the exams. Just a note-he looks at your class position while grading. So, don't panic if your marks in the exams appear low since the only thing that matters is your class position. Also, another piece of advice, try to think of project ideas from the very first.
